questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body is thrown vertically upward with velocity u. The maximum height reached is:
questions.explanation: At maximum height v=0. Using v²=u²-2gH: 0=u²-2gH → H = u²/2g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: From the given ray diagram, identify the type of mirror and the nature of the image formed.
questions.explanation: The ray diagram shows a convex mirror where parallel rays diverge after reflection. The image formed is always virtual, erect, and diminished behind the mirror.
questions.imagePrompt: Clean physics ray diagram of a Convex Mirror. Shows two incident rays (one parallel to principal axis, one directed towards center of curvature) reflecting off the mirror surface. Virtual image formed behind the mirror (shown with dashed lines). Object (arrow) on left, image (smaller dashed arrow) on right behind mirror. Focus F and center C marked behind mirror. Principal axis drawn. Professional optics style.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The unit of electrical resistance is:
questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in Ohm (Ω). R = V/I → 1 Ω = 1 V/A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: Escape velocity v_e = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s for Earth. This is independent of the mass of the escaping object.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the most electronegative element?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table with a Pauling electronegativity of 3.98.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: From the Born-Haber cycle shown, calculate the lattice enthalpy of NaCl.
questions.explanation: Using the Born-Haber cycle: ΔH_f = ΔH_sub + IE + 1/2 D + EA + U. Lattice enthalpy U can be derived from the cycle. U = +786 kJ/mol (endothermic, convention for lattice dissociation).
questions.imagePrompt: Clean chemistry Born-Haber cycle diagram for NaCl. Energy level diagram showing steps: Na(s) → Na(g) sublimation (+108), Na(g) → Na⁺(g) ionization (+496), 1/2 Cl₂(g) → Cl(g) dissociation (+121), Cl(g) → Cl⁻(g) electron affinity (-349), Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → NaCl(s) lattice enthalpy (U = ?). ΔH_f(NaCl) = -411 shown. Arrows up for endothermic, arrows down for exothermic. Professional thermochemistry style.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The process of converting iron ore to iron is called:
questions.explanation: Smelting is the process of extracting metal from its ore by heating with a reducing agent (like coke in blast furnace for iron).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An element with atomic number 17 belongs to which group and period?
questions.explanation: Z=17 is Chlorine: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁵. The outermost shell is n=3 (Period 3). It has 7 valence electrons, belonging to Group 17 (halogens).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The number of subsets of a set containing 4 elements is:
questions.explanation: Number of subsets of a set with n elements = 2ⁿ = 2⁴ = 16.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: From the bar graph shown, which month had the highest sales?
questions.explanation: From the bar graph, March shows the tallest bar with sales of 450 units, making it the month with highest sales.
questions.imagePrompt: Clean math bar graph showing monthly sales data. X-axis: Months (January, February, March, April). Y-axis: Sales (units) from 0 to 500. Bar heights: January=300, February=350, March=450, April=400. Each bar a different color. Grid lines on y-axis. Title 'Monthly Sales Data'. Professional statistics style.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If sin θ = 3/5, then cos θ is (for θ in the first quadrant):
questions.explanation: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. cos²θ = 1 - 9/25 = 16/25. cosθ = 4/5 (positive in first quadrant).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for detoxification in the cell?
questions.explanation: Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification of drugs and poisons, especially in liver cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the structure labeled 'X' in the diagram of the human heart.
questions.explanation: The large artery arising from the left ventricle that carries oxygenated blood to the body is the Aorta.
questions.imagePrompt: Clean biology diagram of the human heart (anterior view, cross-section). Shows four chambers (RA, LA, RV, LV), major blood vessels. The Aorta is labeled with 'X' and an arrow. Pulmonary artery, Superior/Inferior vena cava, pulmonary veins also shown. Oxygenated blood in red, deoxygenated in blue. Labels for all chambers. Professional anatomy style.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of muscle is found in the walls of the intestine?
questions.explanation: Smooth (involuntary, non-striated) muscles are found in the walls of hollow organs like the intestine, stomach, and blood vessels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The largest gland in the human body is:
questions.explanation: The Liver is the largest gland in the human body, weighing about 1.5 kg in adults. It performs over 500 functions.
